title: Midwest diesel rises 5.1% in a week
summary: EIA’s 14 September Midwest diesel benchmark is $6.250/gal, up $0.304 from $5.946. Watershed’s actual surcharge exposure is unknown.
factorRationale: Retail diesel ↑ → carrier fuel surcharges → delivered costs. Exposure 75 assumes truck reliance; severity 70 reflects a 5.1% weekly move. Confidence 70, persistence 70, velocity 80, dependency 80 and substitutability 35 are provisional analyst judgments.
causalPath: Retail diesel ↑ → carrier fuel surcharges → delivered costs. Exposure 75 assumes truck reliance; severity 70 reflects a 5.1% weekly move. Confidence 70, persistence 70, velocity 80, dependency 80 and substitutability 35 are provisional analyst judgments.
verify: Freight contracts, surcharge lag, outbound miles and customer pass-through.
action: Ask logistics and finance to quantify surcharge sensitivity for the next shipping cycle.
trigger: Another >5% weekly rise or contracted transport costs >5% above plan.

title: Grain outlook tightens; specialty basis still unknown
summary: September WASDE projects U.S. total-grain ending stocks of 62.92 Mt versus 65.03 Mt in August. That is a broad context signal, not a popcorn forecast.
factorRationale: Broad grain balance → potential feed/grain pricing → formula costs. All seven factors are uncalibrated proxies (45/55/45/80/45/55/60); popping-grade corn and food-grade contracts can diverge materially.
causalPath: Broad grain balance → potential feed/grain pricing → formula costs. All seven factors are uncalibrated proxies (45/55/45/80/45/55/60); popping-grade corn and food-grade contracts can diverge materially.
verify: Actual grains, specification basis, origin, contracts and inventory cover.
action: Track supplier quotations before changing coverage or formulations.
trigger: Two relevant supplier quotes worsen >10%, or verified cover falls below the approved operating threshold.

title: Traceability planning requires a product-form decision
summary: FDA describes a proposed extension and a congressional direction not to enforce the rule before 20 July 2028. Applicability still depends on covered food and form.
factorRationale: Covered receiving/transformation → KDE/CTE obligations → systems and partner coordination. Scope is not established for Watershed; factors 55/65/65/90/25/70/60 reflect planning exposure rather than a violation.
causalPath: Covered receiving/transformation → KDE/CTE obligations → systems and partner coordination. Scope is not established for Watershed; factors 55/65/65/90/25/70/60 reflect planning exposure rather than a violation.
verify: Food Traceability List applicability at each process stage; exemptions; customer contractual dates.
action: Quality and IT should map covered inputs and data exchanges, retaining product-specific legal review.
trigger: Final regulatory change, customer deadline, or a confirmed gap in an applicable traceability process.

title: Pet formats offer a qualified commercial opening
summary: APPA projects $69.7bn of pet-food and treat sales for 2026. This does not establish unit growth or freeze-dried segment growth.
factorRationale: Pet-category spending → candidate launch budgets → topper/inclusion projects suited to advertised capabilities. Factors 70/60/45/85/45/65/65 reflect an unvalidated sales hypothesis, not Watershed revenue.
causalPath: Pet-category spending → candidate launch budgets → topper/inclusion projects suited to advertised capabilities. Factors 70/60/45/85/45/65/65 reflect an unvalidated sales hypothesis, not Watershed revenue.
verify: Premium segment units, brand launch plans, current capacity and qualified process fit.
action: Build a small list of qualified topper/inclusion prospects and test demand before reserving capacity.
trigger: Documented customer briefs and trial conversion, with confirmed available capacity and validated safety controls.
dateNote: APPA projection publication date unverified; baseline evidence, not a new event on retrieval day.

title: Popcorn expansion is an opportunity to verify
summary: Deer Creek’s public directory now lists Aunt Em’s / Heartland together. The reported equipment transition remains unverified as completed.
factorRationale: Announced process additions → possible new formats → private-label prospects. Factors 70/65/60/85/40/75/60 assume qualification work; no incremental capacity is counted as operational.
causalPath: Announced process additions → possible new formats → private-label prospects. Factors 70/65/60/85/40/75/60 assume qualification work; no incremental capacity is counted as operational.
verify: Equipment ownership, commissioning, production qualification and available slots.
action: Confirm the production milestone before offering new formats or delivery commitments.
trigger: Verified commissioned capacity plus a qualified customer opportunity.

title: Baby-food lead guidance has a material scope exclusion
summary: The FDA final guidance excludes grain-based and freeze-dried snacks. It must not be applied automatically to every toddler product.
factorRationale: SKU classification → applicable contaminant requirements/customer specifications → testing and release criteria. Low velocity 20 reflects an existing rule, not new contamination. Other factors are analytical prioritization.
causalPath: SKU classification → applicable contaminant requirements/customer specifications → testing and release criteria. Low velocity 20 reflects an existing rule, not new contamination. Other factors are analytical prioritization.
verify: Each SKU’s form, age positioning, state rules and customer specifications.
action: Keep contaminant controls; have Quality document the correct guidance scope by SKU.
trigger: Changed FDA/state requirements or an actual out-of-spec result; then use the approved food-safety response process.
